problems.title: Held-out evaluation success influences retries and candidate selection
problems.source_location: Section 3.4, PDF p. 6; Section 4, Evaluation Benchmarks, PDF p. 7; Appendix C, Algorithm 1, PDF p. 19.
claim: Section 4, PDF p. 7, reserves held-out tests for assessment, while Section 3.4 and Appendix C, Algorithm 1, use task-visible feedback. Released datasets_utils.py, lines 173–260, separates public test_list from held-out eval_test_list. eg_cfg_session_manager.py, solve_problem_with_eg_cfg_wrapper and solve_single_problem, lines 491–731, instead use held-out success to stop retries and guidance search.
analysis: Let the public test require \(f(0)=0\), satisfied by both candidate \(A:f(x)=0\) and candidate \(B:f(x)=x\), generated in that order. A held-out requirement \(f(1)=0\) makes the controller stop at \(A\), while changing only that held-out requirement to \(f(1)=1\) makes it continue and select \(B\). Candidate and attempt count depend on held-out feedback even when the held-out text never enters a prompt. This is a source-level selection argument, not a new model-generation run.
result: The inspected release performs test-dependent selection. This known release-level concern does not by itself establish the historical benchmark's affected fraction or a corrected score.
assumptions: The finding is restricted to the identified paper version and identified released component; published experiment provenance is not inferred from public code alone.
repair: Use only task-visible feedback for selection and retries, reserving the held-out tests for one final assessment of the selected candidate.
Known evaluation-selection issue independently reproduced by the proposed clarification; historical table impact remains unresolved.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a demonstrated local release/specification mismatch. Its use in the table-producing runs and any substantial effect on the core scientific conclusion have not been established, so Minor is appropriate.

problems.title: Top-five zero filling can change the token selected by the stated CFG rule
problems.source_location: Sections 3.2–3.3, Eqs. (13)–(14), PDF p. 6; Algorithm 2, lines 29–31, PDF p. 19; released endpoint top-five path.
claim: The token rule in Sections 3.2–3.3, Eqs. (13)–(14), PDF p. 6, and Algorithm 2, lines 29–31, p. 19, applies guidance and takes the resulting argmax. The endpoint implementation requests only five token log probabilities (consts.py:\(215\), inference_endpoint_utils.py:\(432\)–\(472\)). model_utils.py:\(57\)–\(67\) creates a zero vector for the vocabulary and fills only returned probabilities. probs_utils.py:\(38\)–\(48\) applies guidance to those reconstructed vectors.
analysis: For six tokens, take full positive probability vectors

Both sum to one. At \(\gamma=1/2\), the full rule assigns token \(6\) weight \(\sqrt{0.0094}\approx0.09695\), greater than every competing weight (at most \(\sqrt{0.00225}\approx0.04743\)). At \(\gamma=3\), its weight is \(0.94^3/0.01^2=8305.84\), again uniquely largest. The endpoint zero-fills token \(6\) in the prior because it lies outside that prior’s top five. The outer factor in \(\widetilde P_i[(\widetilde P_{c,i}+\epsilon)/(\widetilde P_i+\epsilon)]^\gamma\) then makes its guided mass zero. Epsilon inside the ratio cannot restore it. The explicitly optimized \(\gamma=1\) path and local full-logit path remain valid countercontrols.
result: This is a supported local finding within the stated source/formulation scope. Its effect on the paper's aggregate experimental results remains unmeasured.
assumptions: The finding is restricted to the identified paper version and identified released component; published experiment provenance is not inferred from public code alone.
repair: For available full positive distributions, use the stated log score \((1-\gamma)\log P_i+\gamma\log P_{c,i}\). If only truncated probabilities are available, identify the sparse approximation explicitly; the full-distribution guarantee is unavailable.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a demonstrated local release/specification mismatch. Its use in the table-producing runs and any substantial effect on the core scientific conclusion have not been established, so Minor is appropriate.
problems.existing_correction_status: A local correction or qualification is proposed where specified; author adoption is not established.

impact_rationale: The held-out selection controller and truncated CFG endpoint differ from the declared protocol, but their historical use and effect on the central benchmark comparisons are unestablished. The gamma-one and full-logit controls remain valid; the current paper-level impact is Minor.
